title: Stabilize bimodal tokenflow with conservative prefetcher and immediate customer mitigations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported recurring TTFT spikes and tokens/sec collapses over the last 72 hours. Spike pattern is bimodal: short interactive sessions exhibit expected token emission, while long-context sessions (multi-kB prompts with streaming) experience a dramatic falloff in per-tenant throughput after ~12s. Impact: user-facing time-to-first-token regressions, elevated tail latency alerts, and customer escalations to support and CSMs. Root hypothesis: an aggressive prefetch scheduling heuristic combined with heterogeneous kernel selection + KV cache churn leads to atomic-prefetch bursts that evict working sets for long sessions and trigger scheduler backpressure, cascading into tokenrate collapse. Goals: 1) ship an emergency conservative prefetch throttle to eliminate atomic prefetch bursts, 2) add per-session prefetch budgets and priority-aware admission, 3) deploy canary with telemetry to validate effect on TTFT and tokens/sec, 4) provide customers immediate mitigations and a rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary shows >=40% reduction in TTFT spikes and tokens/sec variance for affected customers vs baseline; 2) No regression in median latency for short sessions; 3) Telemetry surfaces per-tenant prefetch budget usage and eviction events; 4) Rollout flag allows immediate rollback without restart.
playbook: Immediate triage: (1) flip per-customer routing to fallback-variant (smaller context) for 2 highest-severity customers; (2) enable conservative-prefetch feature flag in hosted canary region and Dedicated pilot; (3) open an on-call bridge and notify SRE/CSM. Medium-term: integrate per-session budget accounting, add priority-aware admission to scheduler, and extend KV cache metrics (evictions, working set churn). Long-term: revise kernel selection scoring to be cognizant of prefetch impact on long sessions.
notes: Repro steps captured in triage: reproducer harness with 20 concurrent long-context streams reproduces tokens/sec collapse within 8-15s. Attaching trace ids to observability dashboard for correlation. We observed kernel-change events correlated with a spike in prefetch ops and a 30-60ms GC-like stall on the worker. Hypothesis validated in narrow perf experiment (branch prefetched-guard) showing stabilization for synthetic traffic but minor throughput loss for small sessions; hence the conservative approach.
